_comment: The one verdict. Every mutation here is a way of claiming more than the evidence supports, in one direction or the other: a favourable answer on absence leaves a toolhead running old firmware while the panel says it is fine, and an unfavourable one sends someone to reflash a healthy board during a print. The ordering is as load-bearing as the rules - a measurement that a version string can overrule is not a measurement.

mutations.name: a device that cannot talk to this host is not judged on its version
an offline device is never a verdict
a board in its bootloader is a yes, not an unknown
offline and bootloader state outrank a matching digest
the measurement is consulted before the version string
a digest that disagrees is reported rather than shrugged off
an artifact we could not describe is absence, not mismatch
a disowned cmake sidecar cannot prove its old image current
a cmake image rebuilt behind us cannot prove itself current either
a device that reported no digest is not compared as if it had
mutations.find: if info is None or not info.has_digest() or not expected:
mutations.replace: if info is None or not expected:

mutations.name: an empty reported version says as little as a missing one
a screen with no checkout behind it gets no verdict
a build from an uncommitted tree is never proven current
shas are compared on the shorter of the two, not the reported one
a differing commit is reported rather than passed over
a bare release string with no tree left on its tag is not current
a stamp we did not build is reported
a matching literal with no record behind it is amber, not green
a record naming a hash from another build is not ignored
